tagline: The Wouri estuary at Douala and the volcanic coast of Limbe and Kribi on the Gulf of Guinea.
summary: Cameroon's marine-mobility opportunity centres on the sheltered Wouri estuary at Douala — the country's largest city and principal port — and the scenic volcanic coast to the west and south. Limbe sits beneath Mount Cameroon on a dramatic black-sand shore, and Kribi to the south combines a deep-water port with resort beaches. The Wouri estuary and the near-shore pockets give protected water, while the open Gulf of Guinea carries swell. It is an estuary-and-coast starter market anchored on Douala's waterfront and the Limbe–Kribi leisure coast.
why_marine_mobility: Douala's Wouri estuary is busy by road but direct by water, and the Limbe and Kribi coasts are scenic near-shore pockets the road serves slowly. Navier's Pioneer II flies the sheltered estuary and near-shore hops silent and zero-emission, while the Quanta-LR's range opens the longer Douala–Limbe–Kribi coastal dimension along the Gulf of Guinea.

demand_signals.label: Douala & the Wouri estuary
demand_signals.note: Douala is Cameroon's economic capital and principal port on the sheltered Wouri estuary, with heavy road congestion between waterfront districts.

demand_signals.label: Limbe volcanic coast
demand_signals.note: Limbe's black-sand beaches beneath Mount Cameroon are a leisure draw on a scenic near-shore stretch west of Douala.

demand_signals.label: Kribi deep-water port & beaches
demand_signals.note: Kribi combines a new deep-water port with resort beaches south of Douala, drawing logistics and leisure investment.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling tier across the Wouri estuary linking Douala's waterfront districts on sheltered water.
Scenic near-shore leisure runs along the Limbe volcanic coast for the domestic leisure market.
A Douala–Kribi coastal dimension on the Quanta-LR linking the two port cities along the Gulf of Guinea.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Wouri estuary hops and the Limbe near-shore runs sit within the 70 nm all-electric range on sheltered water, needing only a berth pedestal.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The estuary is Pioneer II territory; the longer Douala ↔ Limbe (~30 nm) and Douala ↔ Kribi (~80 nm) coastal legs are Quanta-LR hybrid corridors where the range and the more open Gulf of Guinea favour the hybrid drivetrain.

signature_routes.label: Douala ↔ Kribi (Gulf of Guinea corridor, Quanta-LR)

transit_planning: For the Port Autonome de Douala or a Littoral regional authority: a clean, zero-emission water tier on the Wouri estuary and the Limbe–Kribi coast, additive to road, as a starter network to validate demand.
competitive_landscape: The Wouri estuary carries informal boat traffic and there is no scheduled fast passenger service on the estuary or the Limbe–Kribi coast. Movement is by congested road with no foiling or zero-emission tier, leaving greenfield room on the sheltered estuary.
regulatory_note: Marine activity falls under Cameroon's maritime authority and the ports of Douala and Kribi, with the sheltered Wouri estuary simplifying near-shore operation while the open Gulf of Guinea carries swell. Cameroon's port-development priorities support a clean estuary-and-coast starter tier.
seasonality: The Gulf of Guinea off Cameroon is warm year-round with a long wet season (roughly March–November, heaviest June–September) and a drier December–February window; the sheltered Wouri estuary is operable year-round while the open coast is calmest in the drier months.
